text:
**For a 1,000Wh power station, plan on about 300-350W of solar to refill it from empty in one good sunny day, or about 200W if you're fine with a day and a half.**

The basic formula is panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75 (real-world losses) = Wh per day.

| Panel | Daily output (4.5 sun hrs, 70%) | Time to refill 1,000Wh |
|---|---|---|
| 100W | ~315Wh | ~3 days |
| 200W | ~630Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400W | ~1,260Wh | Under a day |

(Table from [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/); [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station) gives the same 200W ≈ 630Wh figure.)

**Panel watts to refill in one day, by sun conditions** ([Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):
- 3 peak sun hours: ~450W
- 4 hours: ~340W
- 5 hours: ~270W
- 6 hours: ~230W

Winter is much harder. [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) estimates about 300W in summer but 700W or more in a northern winter.

**Things to check before buying:**
- **Station solar input limit:** Panels beyond the limit add nothing. Many 1,000Wh-class stations accept 400-800W, but some cap at 200W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)). Look up your model.
- **Voltage:** The panels' open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds voltage ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** Panels usually have MC4 connectors, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
- **Running loads while charging:** Net charging is solar input minus whatever you're drawing, so recharging will be slower.
- **Aiming the panels:** Re-aiming toward the sun a few times a day can add 20-30% ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

One of the search results, a product page for a 400W ALLPOWERS panel, contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a discount code and an affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I've left it out and am not recommending that panel based on it.

If you tell me which power station you have and roughly where you'll use it, I can narrow this to a specific panel size and compatible options.
